paper_metadata.title: Simultaneously increasing the strength and ductility of a Ni-Co-based superalloy via dual-heterostructure design

evidence.quote: Ni-Co-based superalloys are recognized as promising materials for the turbine discs of next-generation aero-engines, but the internal strength-ductility trade-off limits their applications.
In this study, conventional rolling and heat treatments are employed to produce a dual HS Ni-Co-based superalloy.

evidence.quote: the HS sample demonstrates a harmonic heterostructure, comprising ultrafine grains (UFGs, < 1 μm) and fine grains (FGs, > 1 μm). Fig. 2 b and c reveal that the volume fractions of UFGs and FGs are 44.4 % and 55.6 %, respectively.
The proportion of Σ3 twin boundaries (peak at ~60◦) is 26.4 %, while that of large angle grain boundaries (LAGBs, > 10◦) is 85.0 %. This evidence suggests that the HS sample is fully recrystallized.
As the applied strain increases, much elevated GND density values are found near the UFG-FG GBs, which supports that GNDs are piled up near the hetero-zone boundary.

It is worthy to note that although the maximum GND density values varied at different GBs, it consistently reverts to the mean value over the same span of distance, which is about 0.5 μm. Such a zone with a high strain gradient was named interface-affected zone (IAZ) firstly [24], and later renamed hetero-zone boundary affected region (HBAR) [20].
